output: – President Obama is wrapping up his final overseas trip as president with a warning against "crude nationalism" from Donald Trump, CNN reports. Speaking in Greece, Obama said he recognized an "anger and fear in the American population" that Trump tapped into to win the presidency. He said Trump had tapped into a "troubling" strain of rhetoric that plays on Americans' fears of globalization. Obama also urged Trump to protect Dreamers, illegal immigrants brought to the US as children. “I will urge the president-elect and the incoming administration to think long and hard before they are endangering the status of what for all practical purposes are American kids,” Obama said. Obama defended his 2012 executive order to protect young immigrants brought here illegally as children, saying "by definition, if they’re part of this program, they are solid, wonderful young people of good character."

– Democratic Sen. Joe Manchin of West Virginia says he will vote to confirm GOP Sen. Jeff Sessions as the next attorney general, the Hill reports. Sessions needs a simple majority in the Senate to confirm him. Manchin is one of several Democrats in vulnerable seats, with Democratic seats in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Florida, and Ohio also up for grabs. All five states voted Trump, with Pennsylvania turning red for the first Republican presidential candidate since 1988. Republicans could hold a filibuster-proof majority after mid-term elections if they win those 10 seats. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell has also announced he supports Sessions for attorney general. Sessions was the first senator to endorse Trump.
